text.p: West Indies batsman Brian Lara was dismissed in controversial circumstances as Australia boosted their victory hopes in the second cricket test on Tuesday.
Lara, the world record holder for the highest score in test and first-class cricket, fell for one in a top order collapse on the fifth and final day at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
Chasing a victory target of 340, West Indies were 152 for four at lunch, still needing 188 runs to win with six wickets in hand.
After being reduced to 35 for three at one stage, West Indies' fortunes were revived by Shivnarine Chanderpaul and Carl Hooper.
But wrist spinner Shane Warne broke their 117-run fourth wicket partnership by bowling Chanderpaul for 71 in the final over before lunch in a vital breakthrough for the home side.
The middle order pair adopted a positive approach despite their team's dire predicament, opting to attack the bowling rather than defend their wickets.
West Indies' survival now rests largely in the hands of Hooper, who remained 47 not out at lunch.
Lara, his side's most influential player, was caught behind by wicketkeeper Ian Healy, but television replays raised doubt as to whether the ball carried.
Umpire David Shepherd delayed his decision for several seconds to consult with his colleague Darrell Hair.

The dismisssal gave fast bowler Glenn McGrath his second wicket for the innings after he trapped opener Sherwin Campbell leg before wicket for 15. Four balls later, Warne accounted for opener Robert Samuels for 16.
Australia led by 27 runs on first innings after scoring 331 and dismissing West Indies for 304. The home side declared their second innings on 312 for four after tea on Monday.
